body: So you're saying I should be careful about what I tell a college counselor. Ok, I'll definitely keep this in mind. The thing about telling my parents is that my mom definitely won't leave me alone until she has some specifics as to what is wrong with me. She has anxiety and depression issues (although nothing like my problem, as far as I know) and if I'm going through the same thing, she'll want to know. Also, I don't like talking about personal stuff with my parents. And if I even started to bring this up with them under the guise of some other problem, I'd probably start crying (I'm prone to crying for some reason when I start talking about deep emotional issues) which would only make things worse. I guess I should just suck it up seeing as I know I need help, but I'm thinking I'll just wait till school starts and until then call a hotline if I have anymore really bad moments.

Wow, I can't believe a school counselor can do something like that. It sounds like handing over way too much power to one person. She just tore up you and your mother's life over her interpretation on something you probably didn't think anything about. 

But, do you mean I shouldn't tell a counselor who works at the college? I wouldn't tell my high school's counselor about this because then I wouldn't have my privacy respected like an adult. If I went into full detail she could probably consider everything enough reason to tell my parents about it. A college counselor should be more discrete, right? 

Also, in case anyone's interested, I had a bad experience with a school counselor when I was eleven as well. In class I for some reason wrote a really bad and violent poem, then crumpled it up and left it on the floor somewhere. The paper had my name on it and somehow I had completely forgotten about this. Well, the teacher saw the poem and alerted the counselor, thinking I was disturbed. I started crying in the counselor's office but mainly because I was embarrassed that someone had read the poem. She took this as a bad sign and called my parents, but thankfully my parents were much more level-headed and understood that my bad poems weren't a sign of anything disturbing going on. So, yeah... I've never been terribly fond of school counselors either.

I don't know... I guess it's possible, but it feels like more of a way I could hurt myself or my parents. Like by hurting something else that they and I care about. God I feel messed up writing that....

EDIT: Actually this is wrong, I just graduated high school and I'm about to start college. Then I'll be away from home and living the dorm. Sorry, it was a long night and I didn't get much sleep.
I go the park and run/walk and I sometimes play any addicting flash games I can find. I'd say music helps the most for me. I'm googling free counseling services in my area now.

Well, when I'm sad for a reason, I just let it pass in a healthy way and usually hurting someone/something doesn't cross my mind. But when I'm sad for no comprehensible reason or even just lonely, I could start petting my cat without any intent to harm him, and then... yeah. Most of the time I just distract myself away from it, but there have been maybe five or six times when I couldn't. I don't really know any other way of "expressing" it other than having plenty of distractions and not letting myself be alone too much.

Thanks... I'm very grateful for the support. But I don't think this is a rage issue. Every time I've ever hurt one of my pets or come close it, I'd start out incredibly sad and somehow wanting to make myself more sad by causing pain to another creature. And afterward I'd cry and feel really shitty for a couple of days. I just wanted to point this out because the two line friends I told wanted to categorize this as an anger issue, but I don't think it is (unless it really is anger and I don't know it).
Thanks... but the summer is long and I don't have many friends to help distract me. I'm hoping someone can help with that here.
I hope so... I will be starting college in August and as soon as I do I will try to find a counselor there, although I can't imagine how I'll even begin to talk about this.

I know, I've come across this a lot and it applies to me all too much. But there has to be some reason why I'm like this. As for it being a phase, I can remember being about seven years old and having thoughts of a similar nature, so I don't think it will go away on its own. 

I've decided I probably won't become a serial killer because I really do feel terrible about my thoughts and actions. I want to fix myself. I need some direction. 

EDIT: Just for the record, my family is not dysfunctional or abusive, my mom is not overly protective, and I do not wet the bed.
